Window washing

Exterior Window Cleaning in Monroe, West Monroe & Ruston

Hand-washed glass, frames and sills — not just a spray-down from the ground. Streak-free, and done carefully around screens, seals and trim.

Call or Text for a Free Estimate Other ways to reach us

What’s included

  • Exterior glass, hand-washed and squeegeed rather than blasted with a pressure washer.
  • Frames and sills, where the dirt film, cobwebs and dead bugs actually collect.
  • Screens on request — pulled, rinsed and put back, so they don’t redeposit dust on glass you just paid to clean.

Windows are one of the few exterior jobs where high pressure is the wrong tool. Force water at an older window and you can push it past the seal or damage the glazing. So this is hand work.

Spring pollen is the reason most people call

Pine pollen coats everything in this part of Louisiana for a few weeks each spring, and glass shows it worse than anything else — a yellow-green haze you notice from inside every time the sun hits it. Washing once the pollen drop is finished gets you clear windows for the rest of the year.

Book it with a house wash

Windows and house washing belong on the same visit. We wash the siding first, then do the glass — otherwise the runoff from the walls lands on windows we just cleaned. Add flowerbed cleanup and the whole front of the house gets handled in one trip.

Questions

Window washing questions we get asked

Do you clean the inside of the windows too?

Our standard window work is exterior glass, frames and sills. If you want interiors done as well, say so when you call and we’ll work it into the estimate.

Why do my windows look worse right after the house is washed?

Because the wall behind them just got clean. It’s the same reason a fresh flowerbed makes dingy siding stand out. That’s why we usually recommend booking house washing and window washing together.

What about screens and tracks?

Screens hold a surprising amount of dust and pollen and can re-dirty clean glass the first time it rains. Tell us whether you want them pulled and rinsed and we’ll include it.

How often should windows be washed?

Once or twice a year suits most homes here. Spring — after the pine pollen has finished — is the single best time, since that yellow film is what makes glass look hazy from inside.

How much does it cost?

It depends on how many windows, how many stories, and whether screens and interiors are included. Call or text and we’ll give you a free estimate.
